newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SCHOLAR IS MEMBER OF CONSORTIUM HOPING TO BUY FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHOLAR IS MEMBER OF CONSORTIUM HOPING TO BUY FOREST.

text.p: Irving Scholar, a controversial figure when he controlled Tottenham Hotspur in the 1980s, is part of a three-man consortium hoping to buy Nottingham Forest.
Forest are currently struggling third from bottom of the premier league and are the target of four potential takeover groups.
Scholar, 48, has joined forces with Lawrie Lewis and lifelong Forest supporter Philip Soar, both of whom have made their money in publishing.
A statement issued on behalf of the trio said Scholar would "act as a consultant on footballing matters but will continue to live in Monaco".
They are offering 10 million pounds sterling ($16 million) for the club, with another 20 million pounds ($32 million) available for improvements if they are successful.
Scholar, who rose from estate agent to multi-millionaire property developer, was chairman of Tottenham from 1984 until 1991, organising their flotation on the London stock exchange.
The club ran into financial problems when attempting to branch into the leisure business.

Tottenham were found guilty by the Football Association of making irregular payments to players during his time in charge and were eventually fined 1.5 million pounds ($2.4 million). He then withdrew from football without having to face individual penalty concerning those irregularities.
Nottingham Forest shareholders, who could benefit by 12,OOO pounds ($19,200) each if they accept the bid from Scholar's group, will discuss the proposals at a meeting on Thursday.
